learningObjective: Create, organise, move and delete resources across resource groups and subscriptions safely. Manage subscription settings: resource providers, quotas, directory and billing owner.
engineer: Resource group location: it only says where the group's own details (metadata) are stored. If that region goes down, you can't update the group, but resources in other regions keep running.
No renaming: you can't rename a resource group. Create a new one and move the resources into it.

Before you move resources: validate first (the portal does this for you); move things that depend on each other together, such as a VM with its disks and network card (NIC); check the move-support table, because some types can't move (for example AKS clusters).

During and after a move: both resource groups are locked for changes while the move runs. Roles given directly on a moved resource don't move with it. Resource IDs change. The region stays the same; moving to another region is a different job (Azure Resource Mover or redeploying).
Moving to another subscription: both subscriptions must be in the same Entra tenant, and the target must have the needed resource providers registered.
Deleting a resource group: everything inside is deleted, in the right order. A lock on anything inside stops the delete. az group delete --no-wait returns at once, but the delete can take minutes.

Subscription jobs: register resource providers (such as Microsoft.ContainerInstance or Microsoft.Insights) before you use a service; check and raise quotas (for example vCPUs per VM family per region) under Usage + quotas; rename the subscription; add tags, budgets, policies and roles (RBAC) at subscription level.
Moving a subscription to another Entra tenant (change directory): all its Azure role assignments are deleted for good, managed identities break, and Key Vaults need their tenant updated.
Changing who pays (billing ownership transfer): a separate job. It doesn't change the directory.
Cancelling a subscription: billing stops and the subscription is disabled, so resources can't be reached. You can reactivate it for up to 90 days, then it and its data are deleted.

example.title: Splitting a shared resource group
body: rg-shared holds a web app and a shared storage account. They have different owners and different lifecycles. The team creates rg-web and moves the App Service plan and web app together, because they depend on each other. Then they give roles on the new resource group.
Two roles had been given directly on the web app. They didn't move, so the team creates them again. Scripts that used the old resource ID are updated.

architectureDecisions: Group by lifecycle and owner: put things that are created, changed and deleted together in one resource group, not all VMs in one and all storage in another.
Use subscriptions for strong separation: separate bills, separate quotas, and a problem in one doesn't spread. Use resource groups for each application.
Give roles on the resource group: not on single resources, so moves and redeployments don't leave roles behind.

misconceptions.myth: Resources must be in the same region as their resource group.
misconceptions.reality: No. The group's location only stores its details. Resources can be in any region.

misconceptions.myth: Moving a resource to another resource group moves it to another region.
misconceptions.reality: No. The region stays the same. The resource ID changes.

misconceptions.myth: You can rename a resource group.
misconceptions.reality: No. Create a new one and move the resources.

misconceptions.myth: Moving a subscription to another directory keeps its roles.
misconceptions.reality: No. All role assignments are deleted.

comparisons.difference: Management groups hold subscriptions, for rules and access. Resource groups hold resources inside one subscription.

comparisons.service: AWS accounts and tags / resource groups
comparisons.difference: An AWS account is like an Azure subscription. AWS Resource Groups are just saved tag searches; they don't own resources.

troubleshooting.symptom: Move validation fails with 'resources not in the same resource group' or missing-dependency errors.
troubleshooting.cause: Something the resource depends on wasn't included, or the resources come from several groups.
troubleshooting.fix: Include everything it depends on, and move from one source group at a time.

troubleshooting.cause: The resource provider isn't registered in the subscription.

troubleshooting.symptom: A deployment fails with a QuotaExceeded or OperationNotAllowed vCPU error.
troubleshooting.cause: You've used all your vCPU quota for that VM family in that region.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask for more in Usage + quotas, or pick another size or region.

troubleshooting.symptom: Users lost access after the subscription moved to another tenant.
troubleshooting.cause: Changing the directory deletes all role assignments.
troubleshooting.fix: Give roles again to people in the new tenant.

troubleshooting.cause: Something inside is locked, or a resource in another group depends on something inside.
troubleshooting.fix: Remove the lock or the dependency first.

configuration.limits: Resource groups can't be renamed or put inside each other
Resources keep their region when moved
Quotas are per subscription (and often per region)
configuration.permissions: Owner on the subscription, to change its directory
configuration.prerequisites: Write access on both the source and target resource groups
For moves between subscriptions: same tenant, and providers registered in the target
